_comment: Curated data the model cannot produce, joined against the model at build time.
Two lists, and the split is deliberate.
current_facts    -- present-tense statements about the PINNED release. These generate the
typer project-* rules, so a rule describes what is true at 0.27.2
rather than what changed on the way here.
breaking_changes -- kept only where the change is within a pinned release's own line
(typer 0.27.0) or belongs to the other subject (rich). Typer's
pre-0.27 history was removed deliberately: this repository describes
typer 0.27.2 and says nothing about earlier releases.
Every `rejected` name and every `answer` is checked against symbols.tsv by verify.py -- a row
that rejects a spelling which does not exist teaches an agent that a non-existent API exists,
which is worse than no row at all.

breaking_changes.subject: typer
breaking_changes.before: Metavar printing changed; an argument now renders as `<str>` in the second help column.
breaking_changes.after: Nothing to change. Update any test asserting on the old help text.

breaking_changes.subject: rich
breaking_changes.before: Import time was improved with lazy loading, and `rich.__version__` stopped existing.

breaking_changes.subject: rich
breaking_changes.before: `cell_len` gained a `unicode_version` parameter and a `UNICODE_VERSION` environment variable.
breaking_changes.after: Leave both alone. Setting the variable changes the measured width of characters and reshapes every table containing one.

breaking_changes.subject: rich
breaking_changes.before: `TTY_INTERACTIVE` was added to force interactive mode off or on.
breaking_changes.after: Nothing to change; know it exists when output differs in CI.

breaking_changes.subject: rich
breaking_changes.before: An empty `NO_COLOR` or `FORCE_COLOR` is now considered disabled, and `TTY_COMPATIBLE` was added.
breaking_changes.after: Unset the variable rather than setting it empty; empty no longer means set.

overlap.question: print a line of plain text from a CLI
overlap.why: Both Rich surfaces parse markup, so any bracketed word in the string may be silently deleted. `typer.echo` is literal.

overlap.question: print text I did not write myself
overlap.why: Untrusted text reaching a Console is parsed as markup. Escape it, or pass `markup=False`.

overlap.question: print a table, a panel or anything laid out
overlap.why: `typer.echo` has no concept of a renderable or a width; it writes the string it is given.

overlap.question: colour one line of output
overlap.why: `typer.style` returns a string you still have to echo. A rich `Style` object is not accepted by either Typer function -- they take colour strings.

overlap.question: reuse a colour in several places
overlap.why: `typer.colors.RED` is the plain string "red". It is legal in Rich markup only because the spellings coincide, and it carries no other attributes.

overlap.question: show a progress bar
overlap.why: `typer.progressbar` is the vendored Click one: no columns, no transient mode, and it writes to a stream Rich does not own, so it fights a live Console.

overlap.question: ask the user a question
overlap.why: Both Typer prompts bypass the Console, so under a `Live` or `Progress` the prompt is overwritten. Fine standalone.

overlap.question: exit with a code I choose
overlap.why: `Abort` always exits 1 and prints "Aborted."; `Exit` takes the code.

overlap.question: catch any error Typer raises
overlap.why: `BadParameter` is the only vendored Click exception re-exported at top level; the other six are reached through the `TyperException` ancestor.

overlap.question: assert on CLI output in a test
overlap.why: A recording Console sees only what you printed through it, not what the vendored Click wrote. `CliRunner` also pins the plain formatter's width, though not the Rich one.

overlap.question: control how wide the output is
overlap.why: Width is a property of the Console, not of the thing you print -- and even an explicitly passed width loses to `TERM=dumb`.

overlap.question: get the installed version at runtime
overlap.why: Does not exist at rich 15.0.0. `typer.__version__` does, which makes the asymmetry easy to trip over.

env_vars.name: NO_COLOR
env_vars.effect: Drops colour but keeps other attributes, even with force_terminal and an explicit color_system.

env_vars.name: FORCE_COLOR
env_vars.effect: Treats the stream as a terminal. Yields the `standard` colour system on its own, not truecolor.

env_vars.name: TTY_INTERACTIVE
env_vars.effect: Forces interactive mode off or on, which governs Live and Progress.

env_vars.name: TERM
env_vars.effect: `dumb` overrides a width passed explicitly to the constructor and reports 80.

env_vars.name: COLORTERM
env_vars.effect: `truecolor` or `24bit` raises the colour system above `standard`.

env_vars.name: COLUMNS
env_vars.effect: Sets the width when none was passed. Does not override an explicit width.

env_vars.name: LINES
env_vars.effect: Sets the height when none was passed.

env_vars.name: UNICODE_VERSION
env_vars.effect: Changes how many cells a character measures, reshaping every table containing one. Not covered by `Console(_environ=...)`, and cached, so it is order-dependent too.

env_vars.name: JUPYTER_COLUMNS
env_vars.effect: Width inside a notebook. Never exercised here -- see known limit 6.

env_vars.name: JUPYTER_LINES
env_vars.effect: Height inside a notebook. Never exercised here.

env_vars.name: TERMINAL_WIDTH
env_vars.effect: Fixes the width of Typer's Rich help output. Read once into `MAX_WIDTH`, so setting it after the module is imported does nothing.

env_vars.name: _TYPER_FORCE_DISABLE_TERMINAL
env_vars.effect: Forces Typer's help Console to render as a non-terminal. Private, and named as such.

env_vars.name: PY_COLORS
env_vars.effect: Collapsed into FORCE_TERMINAL at import, alongside FORCE_COLOR.

env_vars.name: GITHUB_ACTIONS
env_vars.effect: Presence forces terminal mode, so help output is coloured in CI logs.

env_vars.name: DATABRICKS_RUNTIME_VERSION
env_vars.effect: Participates in Jupyter detection. Not covered by `Console(_environ=...)`.

refused.why: Output depends on elapsed time and refresh rate; there is no construction that produces stable bytes, and a normalised capture would be a fiction dressed as evidence.
refused.instead: `content/corpus/rich/tests/test_progress.py` -- upstream's own executable statement. Probe `R003` covers the deterministic `disable=True` path.

refused.why: The frame index is a function of elapsed time.
refused.instead: `rich/_spinners.py` is the data table; read the frames rather than a capture of one.

refused.what: Terminal capability negotiation on a real TTY
refused.why: Every probe writes to a `StringIO`, which is not a terminal. What a real TTY negotiates is indexed from source and never asserted.
refused.instead: `catalogs/env-vars.md` for the variables, and `rich/docs/source/console.rst` in the corpus for upstream's account.

refused.why: Lexers and token boundaries belong to Pygments, not Rich. A captured highlight would be a claim about Pygments wearing Rich's name.
refused.instead: The frame -- gutter, line numbers, padding, background -- is stable and indexed. Pygments is pinned at 2.21.0 in `resolved.json`.

refused.why: A real traceback carries absolute paths, an interpreter version and frame counts that differ per machine -- and the paths are a transferability leak into `content/`, not merely a determinism one.
refused.instead: Probe `R002` captures the structure under a synthetic filename, with the normalisation recorded on the row.

refused.why: `_win32_console.py`, `_windows_renderer.py`, `legacy_windows=True` and Typer's conditional `colorama` are never executed. Every probe passes `legacy_windows=False` explicitly, which is part of why they are deterministic.
refused.instead: Indexed from source. A box glyph shown here may be substituted on a legacy Windows console.

refused.why: No probe imports IPython, and `is_jupyter()` is False in all of them.
refused.instead: `content/seams/jupyter.md`, marked `supported: observed-only` for exactly this reason.

refused.why: `shellingham` inspects the parent process and `--install-completion` writes to the user's home directory. Neither is safe or stable to execute in a build.
refused.instead: Indexed from source, plus `typer/docs/tutorial/options-autocompletion.md` in the corpus.

current_facts.subject: typer
current_facts.fact: Typer 0.27.2 carries its own adapted copy of Click at `typer/_click/` and does not depend on the `click` distribution.
current_facts.evidence: Requires-Dist lists shellingham, rich, annotated-doc and colorama (Windows). `click` is absent, and is not in the resolved graph.
current_facts.consequence: An `import click` in a Typer project resolves to an unrelated copy installed for some other reason -- a different library from the one Typer runs -- and it type-checks either way. `typer.main.get_command(app)` returns a `typer._click` Command that no Click plugin accepts.

current_facts.subject: typer
current_facts.fact: At 0.27.2 `typer-slim` is a shallow wrapper around `typer` and requires `rich` and `shellingham` unconditionally.
current_facts.evidence: Its distribution metadata declares both as hard requirements.
current_facts.consequence: Depending on `typer-slim` to keep Rich out of the dependency tree keeps nothing out. Depend on `typer`.
